transcript.note: Coarsened rank-snapping into a compact 9x8 grid by merging contiguous-rank column/row groups that also share a direct edge: colA{4,13,15,11} (west trunk of circular line, edges 4-13,13-15,4-11 all vertical), colB{8,5,3,7} (edges 8-3,5-3,8-7 vertical), colC{16,0,14} (edges 16-0,16-14 vertical); rowD'{14,11,6,7} (edges 11-6,6-7,14-7 horizontal), rowE{8,16,10,12} (orange-line trunk 8-16,16-10,10-12 all horizontal), rowF{3,15,0} (edges 15-3,0-3 horizontal), row{9,5} (edge 9-5 horizontal). Kept vertex 1 and vertex 2 out of their neighbors' row groups (1 separated from {9,5}, 2 separated from row D') specifically to avoid a vertex sitting on the straight line of a non-adjacent edge (1-9 would have put 5 on the segment; 7-2 would have put 14 on the segment). The remaining two edges (1-9, 7-2) are deliberately left diagonal: forcing either into H/V would put an unrelated vertex (5, resp. 14) exactly on the straight segment between the endpoints, which is the same vtxOn trap round 1's design avoided by keeping 1 and 2 out of their neighbours' row groups.
